articles.title: Rising Patient Cash Payments for GLP-1 Medications Impact Employer Plans
articles.summary: An increasing number of patients are paying out-of-pocket cash for GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes medications due to strict employer plan restrictions and prior authorization hurdles. This trend highlights the financial strain of these blockbuster drugs and suggests employees are bypassing traditional PBM benefit channels to secure treatment. For self-funded employers, this shift creates new challenges in tracking total health utilization, managing population health outcomes, and evaluating the true ROI of obesity benefit designs.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Economics; Mon, 05 Oct 2026 18:07:30 GMT

articles.title: Benefits Brokers Pivot Strategy to Combat Soaring Health Plan Costs
articles.summary: Health benefits brokers are actively seeking new advisory strategies and cost-containment solutions as employer health plan expenditures continue to surge. This trend highlights the growing demand among self-funded employers for innovative pharmacy and medical benefit management partners to help control escalating expenses.

articles.title: Bipartisan Congressional Scrutiny Intensifies Against Pharmacy Benefit Managers
articles.summary: Lawmakers from both parties are increasingly targeting pharmacy benefit managers over drug pricing practices and transparency issues. This bipartisan pressure signals potential federal reform that could significantly impact how PBMs operate and contract with self-funded employer health plans. The growing momentum highlights the need for employers to closely monitor legislative developments affecting their pharmacy benefit management strategies.

articles.title: SHARx Warns Self-Funded Employers That Discounts Fail to Control Pharmacy Spend
articles.summary: A new advisory report from SHARx highlights that traditional PBM discount models and rebates are insufficient for controlling total pharmacy spending for self-funded employers. The analysis emphasizes that managing plan costs requires a deeper focus on utilization management, alternative funding strategies, and holistic plan design rather than relying solely on headline discounts. This directly impacts self-funded plan sponsors seeking effective cost-containment solutions amidst rising specialty drug expenses.
articles.source_line: Source: PR Newswire; Mon, 05 Oct 2026 12:08:00 GMT
